newsitem.title: USA: Oxygen generator shipment probed by U.S., France.
newsitem.headline: Oxygen generator shipment probed by U.S., France.

text.p: U.S. and French officials are investigating whether 900 oxygen generators were shipped into the United States aboard Air France, violating a ban on shipping the devices in passenger planes, the Federal Aviation Administration said on Tuesday.
Oxygen generators were implicated in the crash of a ValuJet flight near Miami in May last year that killed 110 people.
Shipment of the generators by passenger planes has been banned since that crash although they can be carried by cargo planes if properly labelled and declared.

"While the alleged shipment appears to have included generators packed in protective metal containers, we are very concerned that they may have been on board a passenger plane," said Cathal Flynn, associate administrator for Civil Aviation Security at the FAA.
"Every shipper and every airline should know by now these shipments are strictly illegal," Flynn said in a statement.
Air France said it could not provide details because an investigation was underway.

"Air France takes federal regulations and safety concerns very seriously and is currently working with both the FAA and the French civil aviation authorities on this investigation," the airline said in a statement from New York.

The FAA said the oxygen generators were undeclared and might have been aboard an all-cargo flight as well as a combination passenger-cargo flight. It said France has a similar prohibition on shipping the generators.
The FAA began its probe June 30 when delivery company Federal Express notified it of a shipment of undeclared generators within the United States that was traced back to Air France.
The oxygen generators are legal when used to supply emergency oxygen masks for passengers in the event of depressurization and are mounted overhead for that purpose.
However, when transported as cargo, the generators have the potential to quickly accelerate a fire.
A source close to the investigation said Air France might have been an unwitting carrier of the generators since the cargo was not declared.
Earlier this year, Continental Airlines Inc. said it had unknowingly transported armed oxygen generators on an uneventful flight from Los Angeles to Houston on April 16.
A Continental contractor, Santa Barbara Aerospace, is still under investigation over the shipment pending a possible enforcement action.

The ValuJet crash brought increased attention to cargo fires. Last month the FAA outlined rules under which a halon gas fire suppression system would be fitted to cargo holds that previously relied on an airtight seal to slow a blaze.
